author: Falyn Stempler
title: Marco Rubio jokes about replacing Karoline Leavitt as press secretary as she takes maternity leave - NewsBreak
text:
By Falyn Stempler ,
1 hours ago Secretary of State Marco Rubio was caught on camera jokingly posing in front of the White House briefing room as White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt is on maternity leave.
Leavitt, 28, announced her temporary departure from the Trump administration on Friday, April 24, about a week ahead of her expected delivery of her second child , which she revealed is a girl. In the interim, various officials are expected to take turns handling her responsibilities rather than designating a formal substitute, the White House confirmed after reports emerged from POLITICO.
The outlet reported that officials ranging from Vice President JD Vance, Cabinet members and even President Donald Trump himself could assume the role while Leavitt remains on maternity leave — which means Rubio's stunt could become a reality in the near future.
• Karoline Leavitt cuts maternity leave short after White House Correspondents' Dinner breach
• Karoline Leavitt's replacement named as she takes a break from White House role
The state secretary was captured on video by Iran International making an "unannounced appearance in the White House briefing room," telling reporters that "he was there to mess with someone and carry out a joke" while Leavitt is on maternity leave.
All communication operations will be overseen by White House Communications Director Steven Cheung, with assistance from Leavitt's team, while she is out of the office.
Leavitt, who gave birth to her first son, Niko, in July 2024 while working on Trump's 2024 presidential campaign, announced her temporary departure via Instagram.
"When my husband and I found out we were expecting another child, my first thought was overwhelming gratitude and joy," she wrote. "My second thought was 'how the heck am I going to do this job, with a toddler, and while pregnant?' Well, 39 weeks later, and we did it. Be back soon."
Among the images attached in the post was a CNN clip where she told reporters that "this will likely be my last gaggle for some time. As you can see, I'm about to have a baby any minute. I will see you guys very soon. I know you'll be in good hands with my team here at the White House."
Before exiting, she joked, "And I know all of you have the president's phone number personally, so I have no doubt you won't have a shortage of statements and news from the building while I'm gone."
However, during her departure, she attended the White House Correspondents' Dinner with her husband, Nicholas Riccio, 60. Before the ceremony, where all hell broke loose after a gunman opened fire, ultimately canceling the event, Leavitt remarked on the president's prepared speech that came under scrutiny.
Before the event, she told reporters about Trump's speech, "It'll be funny. It'll be entertaining. There will be some shots fired tonight in the room." Critics raised their eyebrows about the explosive remark after the shooting unfolded, which prompted her to cut her maternity break short after just three days off.
She posted an update on X on Monday, April 27, confirming her return to work, writing, "I will hold a Press Briefing at 1PM ET today."
